verdict.root_cause: The evidence does not establish a failing mechanism. Nearly every dispatch returned an empty answer: no nginx logs [tr_38611975bcd5], no compose-post logs [tr_f5e3ed08eb82], no nginx traces across a full hour [tr_ebf55ae35440], and no span-metric samples at all for compose-post, home-timeline or user-timeline in either the incident or baseline window [tr_0d99b3b3f553, tr_6a0a1142c89c, tr_73654c07a93e]. The only non-empty signals are nginx's intermittent, non-sustained error ratio with no baseline to compare against [tr_0b7d99223f50] and change records showing that nginx-web-server and compose-post-service were both first created by platform-automation about three minutes before onset [tr_08bfa0bd702e, tr_88ef5ea29f07]. The most defensible reading is that this environment was being brought up from scratch at 16:03 and alerted at 16:06 before the stack had stabilised or begun emitting telemetry; the specialists found no running-state fault to attribute. Naming a culprit service and mechanism on this board would be invention.
verdict.reasoning: A fault class must be inferred from what a service is doing wrong, and here no service produced a signal of doing anything. The change records are the strongest evidence and they point away from every change-driven class: all entries are first creations by platform-automation with no prior version, so there is no artifact to have regressed (bad_deploy), no value edited away from a working one (bad_config), and nothing to roll back [tr_08bfa0bd702e, tr_88ef5ea29f07]. The hang-versus-silence discriminators cannot be applied: process_freeze and network_partition are told apart by whether the culprit logs that it cannot reach anything, and no logs exist for either service queried [tr_38611975bcd5, tr_f5e3ed08eb82]. Nothing in the board shows a no-space-left message, a decode failure, or a saturation signal, so disk_fill, datastore_corruption and resource_exhaustion have no positive support either. The nginx error ratio is explicitly non-sustained with an absent baseline, so it cannot anchor a regression [tr_0b7d99223f50], and the total absence of traces rules out attributing the fault to any named downstream call [tr_ebf55ae35440]. The coincidence of first-creation timestamps three minutes before onset across two independent services is the one coherent pattern, and it is consistent with an environment mid-bring-up rather than a steady-state failure.
open_questions: Whether the empty Loki and Tempo results reflect genuinely silent services or selector/label mismatches and a telemetry collection gap — both the compose-post log query and the nginx trace query carried truncation flags [tr_f5e3ed08eb82, tr_ebf55ae35440], and the span-metric series were equally empty before the incident [tr_0d99b3b3f553].

Pod and container state from Kubernetes events: were the newly created workloads ever Running and Ready, or stuck pulling images, pending scheduling, or crash-looping before writing a first log line? No dispatch queried the orchestrator.

Latency and saturation were never measured for any of the four services; only the error-ratio template was run [tr_6a0a1142c89c, tr_73654c07a93e], so a slow-dependency or resource-pressure mechanism remains untested.
What actually triggered the critical alert at 16:06:34 and which signal it fired on — no evidence on the board reproduces an alertable condition.
Whether the three unmeasured edges crossed by triage hide a backend (post-storage, Redis/Mongo, or a service-discovery layer) that was never dispatched against.

alternatives.root_cause: The whole social-network stack was still completing an automated cold start when the alert fired, so the services had not yet begun serving or emitting telemetry and the alert caught a bring-up transient rather than a fault.
alternatives.why_not: This is the most likely benign reading and is nearly identical to the verdict, but it makes a positive claim of transience that the board cannot confirm: no pod-state or readiness evidence exists, and the services could equally have come up and stayed broken.

alternatives.root_cause: compose-post-service never started successfully after its first creation, so nginx-web-server hung on an unreachable backend and its callers timed out.
alternatives.why_not: A freeze is diagnosed from a silent culprit whose socket still accepts, but here there is no evidence the socket accepted anything, no nginx upstream-timeout lines [tr_38611975bcd5], and no spans showing hanging calls [tr_ebf55ae35440] — the silence is equally explained by a pod that never reached Running or by a telemetry gap that predates onset [tr_0d99b3b3f553].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any observable signal should follow from this proposal. The correct next step is observation, not remediation: query the orchestrator for pod/container state (Running, Ready, ImagePullBackOff, Pending, CrashLoopBackOff) for nginx-thrift and compose-post-service around 16:03:32-16:06:40, and re-run the Loki and Tempo queries with a broader selector (namespace only, no pod regex) to separate a genuinely silent stack from a label/selector mismatch. Either of those would produce the first positive signal this board lacks.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the stack is in fact wedged in a state a container recreate would clear - for example if the orchestrator shows compose-post-service or nginx-web-server stuck in CrashLoopBackOff or started before a dependency was listening. Nothing on this board shows that: the logs that would carry a crash banner are empty [tr_f5e3ed08eb82], and the only non-empty metric is a non-sustained, baseline-less nginx error ratio [tr_0b7d99223f50]. If a pod-state query returns a restart count climbing or a container in a terminal error state, restart_service on that service becomes defensible and this abstention should be revisited immediately.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the environment stays broken while nobody acts, and the alert from 16:06:34 continues unaddressed. The risk of the alternative - acting anyway - is larger and concrete: rollback_image and revert_config both require a prior image tag or prior configuration, and the change history records only first creations for both nginx-web-server [tr_08bfa0bd702e] and compose-post-service [tr_88ef5ea29f07], so there is no prior state to return to and either action would fail or deploy an arbitrary tag. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; with zero logs, zero traces and zero span metrics [tr_f5e3ed08eb82, tr_ebf55ae35440, tr_0d99b3b3f553] there is no such evidence, and recreating a container three minutes into a cold bring-up would reset whatever startup progress exists and destroy the very first log lines a diagnosis depends on.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing is changed. For context on what was declined: a restart or redeploy of nginx-web-server would be seen by every external caller of the edge and by its three downstreams compose-post-service, home-timeline-service and user-timeline-service; a restart of compose-post-service would be seen by nginx-web-server as reset inbound connections. Both would also disturb the as-yet-unmeasured bring-up sequence for the whole social-network namespace.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on the user-facing entry point cannot be dismissed, and no open incident could account for it. The single seed with unmeasured downstream edges gives no basis yet for a fault class.
